name: Negative Approach
label: Touch and Go
lede: John Brannon fronted a Detroit teenage hardcore band that fit ten songs on one seven-inch and an album into 16 minutes 53 seconds, then split before the album came out. Twenty-three years later he was back, and still had no computer.

eras.title: Detroit skate parks, then a Touch and Go sampler
eras.text: John Brannon grew up on Creem, the Stooges and the MC5, and in the summer of 1981 hardcore gave him a way in. He recruited teenagers from Detroit skate parks, and within months the band was on the first Touch and Go record and playing the East Coast.

years.h: A Black Flag show sends John Brannon and Pete Zelewski into a band
years.p: Singer John Brannon and bassist Pete Zelewski start Negative Approach in Detroit in August 1981, after reportedly seeing [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] play, according to CBS News.

years.src: Vice: interview with John Brannon · Metro Times: Three chords · CBS News: Negative Approach headline
years.h: Zelewski out, two brothers and a drummer called Opie in
years.p: [[Rob McCulloch|0071a9c5-d23d-4117-a9d1-656cddcf2fd1]] takes guitar, his brother [[Graham McCulloch|a9cb94ec-b297-44d5-9ea1-dbefe4b26c33]] bass and Chris "Opie" Moore drums. Most of them are 15 or 16 years old.
years.xp: John Brannon told Vice that the band's age was its biggest limit: kids that young couldn't just get in a van and tour. Metro Times says he found his players at Detroit skateboard parks and built an all-ages scene of underground shows for kids like them.

years.h: Lost Cause lands on Touch and Go's Process of Elimination sampler
years.p: It's Negative Approach's first release, on a seven-inch of Midwest hardcore. A three-show run through Boston, New York and Washington, D.C. follows.

years.big: "Fear's going to be on. You guys should come down and we'll destroy NBC."
years.src: Vice: interview with John Brannon · Metro Times: Three chords
years.h: Belushi invites the hardcore kids to NBC
years.p: John Belushi brings a crew of hardcore kids to [[Fear|5e6512dd-160b-4512-a4b4-2c30fa894a08]]'s Halloween 1981 set on Saturday Night Live. John Brannon ends up in the slam pit, with a mohawk Belushi gave him, and grabs a microphone on live TV.
years.xp: That's Brannon's account of Belushi's invitation to Vice. He was roadying for the [[Necros|a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8]] at the time. [[Tesco Vee|b988565c-c8c3-4491-b9ec-131cdb0df9be]] of [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]] was in the same pit. Metro Times quotes Brannon on the haircut: "Belushi gave me a mohawk."

eras.title: Ten songs, one seven-inch
eras.text: The debut crammed ten songs onto one small record, none long enough to catch your breath. Onstage, John Brannon treated every gig as the band against the room.

years.src: Wikipedia: Negative Approach (EP) · Metro Times: Three chords · Austin Chronicle: Ready to Fight
yt: Live at the Club House, Detroit, October 9, 1982
years.h: The Negative Approach EP crams ten songs onto one 7-inch
years.p: Recorded in April 1982 with [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]] producing for Touch and Go. Pressure lasts nine seconds, and the longest track runs under two minutes.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the first pressing was 3,000 copies. The cover borrows its imagery from The Exorcist, according to Metro Times. Larissa Strickland, later of [[Laughing Hyenas|a3e6d60a-34ff-4d99-8397-2db6b5b2333e]], booked the band's early shows and helped write Lead Song, Brannon told the Austin Chronicle: "She booked us. She helped write 'Lead Song' on the 7″."

years.src: Metro Times: Three chords · Metro Times: Negative Approach consider · Threat Base: Minor Threat
yt: Negative Approach live at the Freezer Theater, 1982
years.h: Bricks through windows at the Freezer Theater, and then no Freezer
years.p: Negative Approach opens for [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] on June 18, 1982, at the Freezer Theater on Cass Avenue. A riot breaks out in the parking lot, and Metro Times says windows were smashed, people were arrested and the Freezer never reopened.
years.xp: Brannon's summary to Metro Times: "Bricks through windows, blood. That was the end of the Freezer Theatre." The 2010 story puts [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]] on the same bill; the 2016 story calls it the Freezer's final show. The Minor Threat date comes from the band's show archive.

q: Me and the band against the audience.
years.src: Metro Times: Three chords · Vice: interview with John Brannon
years.h: Every Negative Approach gig is the band against the room
years.p: John Brannon runs the shows as a confrontation, and fights in the crowd become part of the draw.
years.xp: Metro Times quotes Brannon on the idea, and the 1982 set above shows it. Thirty years on, Vice titled its Brannon interview "There's no shortage of blood and crazy motherfuckers."

eras.title: Tied Down, then torn apart
eras.text: Negative Approach made its only album in the summer of 1983 and split before it came out. The crowds had grown, the fights had grown with them, and the drummer wanted out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tied Down · Metro Times: Three chords
yt: Live at the Graystone, Detroit, September 18, 1983
years.h: Tied Down is the only album, and it runs 16 minutes 53 seconds
years.p: Ten songs, recorded in August 1983 at Multi Track Studios in Redford, Michigan, with Corey Rusk producing and Lloyd Grace engineering.
years.xp: The line-up was John Brannon, Rob McCulloch on guitar, Graham McCulloch on bass and Chris "OP" Moore on drums. Rusk also shot the photos for the lyric sheet. Metro Times says the band had already split by the time the record came out.

years.big: "I was getting sick of the fact that it started getting popular."
q: I was getting sick of the fact that it started getting popular.
years.src: Austin Chronicle: Ready to Fight · Metro Times: Three chords
years.h: Negative Approach breaks up a week before its Texas dates with Big Boys
years.p: The original line-up falls apart on the Tied Down tour, a week before three planned Texas dates with [[Big Boys|fde1cff2-5a7b-4e8c-9666-110fa90500fb]]. Drummer Chris "Opie" Moore blames the growing crowds and the fights.
years.xp: Brannon told the Austin Chronicle the Texas shows never happened: "We broke up before that. Only a handful of people saw the shows." He told Metro Times hardcore had run its course for him, and that some fans were showing up for the violence, not the songs.

years.h: Brannon's all-new Negative Approach lasts a handful of dates
years.p: After Tied Down, John Brannon puts together an entirely new line-up, which dissolves after a handful of dates in 1984, according to CBS News.

years.h: Graham McCulloch takes his bass to The Meatmen in D.C.
years.p: Bassist Graham McCulloch joins [[Tesco Vee|b988565c-c8c3-4491-b9ec-131cdb0df9be]]'s [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]], now based in Washington, D.C. with ex-[[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] guitarists [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] and [[Lyle Preslar|c1b9b78e-691f-424d-8ce1-53c87c24d299]]. He stays until 1988.

years.h: Laughing Hyenas start in Ann Arbor with Larissa Strickland on guitar
years.p: John Brannon and guitarist Larissa Strickland form [[Laughing Hyenas|a3e6d60a-34ff-4d99-8397-2db6b5b2333e]] in late 1984. Their first show is in April 1985, and the band runs until 1995.

eras.title: Twenty years of other bands
eras.text: Negative Approach's two records became passwords among hardcore fans. John Brannon spent the years fronting other bands while the McCulloch brothers and Opie Moore moved on.

years.h: Total Recall puts the EP and Tied Down on one release
years.p: Touch and Go's 1992 collection gives a generation that only knew the band from tape a proper copy.
years.xp: By then the members were scattered. Opie Moore and Rob McCulloch played together in the alt-rock band Crossed Wire. Graham McCulloch went from The Meatmen to Earth 18 with Void's Bubba Dupree, then Mother May I. Moore later went solo as a roots singer-songwriter.

years.h: Easy Action puts Harold Richardson and Ron Sakowski behind Brannon
years.p: After Laughing Hyenas end in 1995, John Brannon fronts the Detroit rock band Easy Action, with guitarist [[Harold Richardson|b6e5c3cb-d902-4c81-ad4e-9c2c6e546826]] and bassist [[Ron Sakowski|0a176fe9-0c15-44a6-a227-ef345f441acb]]. Their debut album is out on Reptilian in 2001.

years.h: Ready to Fight digs up demos and live tapes from 1981-83
years.p: Reptilian's Ready to Fight: Demos, Live and Unreleased 1981–83 is the first new Negative Approach material in more than twenty years.

eras.title: Corey Rusk calls
eras.text: Touch and Go's Corey Rusk asked, and John Brannon said yes to something he never expected to do. The reunion band was half original, half Easy Action, and its first show drew the biggest crowd of its life.

years.src: Austin Chronicle: Ready to Fight · Metro Times: Three chords · CBS News: Negative Approach headline
years.h: Brannon and Moore reunite, minus the McCulloch brothers
years.p: John Brannon and Opie Moore re-form for Touch and Go's 25th anniversary, with Easy Action's Harold Richardson on guitar and Ron Sakowski on bass. Metro Times says they practiced twice, in Richardson's basement.
years.xp:
Brannon told the Austin Chronicle he had lost touch with Rob and Graham McCulloch. Of one phone call about the reunion: "By the second phone call he was calling me a fucking asshole."

Sakowski had played bass in Laughing Hyenas and Easy Action; CBS News also lists him as a former [[Necros|a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8]] bassist.

years.cap: John Brannon in the pit, May 2007, the reunion's first full year
years.src: Vice: interview with John Brannon · Metro Times: Three chords
years.h: Twenty-three years on, Negative Approach plays Chicago for 7,000
years.p: At Touch and Go's 25th anniversary weekend, the band plays a bill of the label's reunited acts, including [[Killdozer|6a2f72b1-d660-409e-b190-6470157d3a38]]. Metro Times puts the outdoor crowd at about 7,000, the band's biggest ever.
years.xp: Brannon told Vice he never expected to put the band back together, and that "there were 6,000 people there." Metro Times says 7,000; the first show since 1983 was Corey Rusk's idea.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas · CelebrityAccess: Guitarist · Austin Chronicle: Ready to Fight
years.h: Larissa Strickland dies at 46
years.p: Laughing Hyenas guitarist Larissa Strickland, John Brannon's former partner, dies in North Port, Florida. CelebrityAccess reported an apparent overdose of the prescription drug Xanax.
years.xp: The Austin Chronicle wrote that Strickland booked Negative Approach's early shows, co-wrote a song on their first record and shaped the band.

years.h: London, then All Tomorrow's Parties on the Stooges' bill
years.p: Negative Approach plays London on December 7 and All Tomorrow's Parties on December 10, a bill with [[The Stooges|794c6bf2-3241-416f-9b8f-24e2d84a1c4b]] and the [[MC5|08b736bb-1c82-40b4-8b0b-49e2182a067a]], the Detroit bands John Brannon grew up on.

years.h: Tesco Vee gets Negative Approach as his backing band
years.p: Negative Approach plays a 30-minute set in Detroit behind [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]] frontman [[Tesco Vee|b988565c-c8c3-4491-b9ec-131cdb0df9be]], who says it got him performing again.

years.cap: Negative Approach at Southpaw, Brooklyn, November 2009
years.h: April in the Northeast, June in Europe
years.p: Negative Approach tours the Northeast and then Europe. John Brannon later tells Vice the band has been to Europe five times since the reunion.

years.cap: Negative Approach at St. Andrew's Hall, Detroit, July 31, 2010
years.h: A book named after one of their songs gets a Detroit party
years.p: At St. Andrew's Hall in Detroit, Negative Approach plays Tony Rettman's Detroit hardcore history Why Be Something That You're Not, titled after one of their songs.

years.h: Taang! digs up the 1984 line-up on Nothing Will Stand in Our Way
years.p: Taang! Records releases unreleased 1984 recordings from the short-lived second line-up. The band plays Fun Fun Fun Fest in Austin the same month.

eras.title: Still no email
eras.text: The reunion was supposed to be one show. A decade on, Negative Approach was headlining clubs and German metal festivals, and John Brannon still said he had no computer.

years.cap: John Brannon at the Amphetamine Reptile anniversary party, Grumpy's, Minneapolis, July 2013
years.h: Brannon tells Vice he never planned a reunion
years.p: John Brannon says he never expected to put Negative Approach back together, and that he has no computer or email.
years.xp: On the computer: "I don't have a computer. I'm stuck in the '70s. I don't fuck with that shit." On the point of it all: "It's not about the money. It's about going out and fucking people up."

years.cap: Negative Approach at Logo, Hamburg, October 2015
years.h: After a Third Man show, Brannon says it's time for new songs
years.p: After a show at Jack White's Third Man Records in Detroit, John Brannon tells Metro Times it's time for new Negative Approach songs, with Opie Moore coming in from Brooklyn. Wacken Open Air is booked for summer.

years.h: A documentary puts Detroit hardcore on screen
years.p: Dope, Hookers and Pavement arrives during the pandemic, with members of Negative Approach, [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]] and [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] telling the Detroit hardcore story.

years.cap: Negative Approach at Hafenklang, Hamburg, May 2024
years.h: Back on the road in 2023 with OFF!, Punch and Circle Jerks
years.p: John Brannon is still out front. CBS News has the band headlining Albany's Ivy Room on July 17 that summer.
